patch_description:
This implementation replaces expensive full-region validation and simulated annealing with a monotone frontier-peeling search.

It grows color `0` only from the outside-connected frontier, so zero-connectivity is guaranteed structurally. For each attempted removal or recoloring, it incrementally updates only the affected adjacency-pair counts. Connectivity of the removed ward is checked using a small articulation-style BFS between the same-colored neighbors of the changed cell, instead of BFS-checking both entire affected regions.

The solver repeatedly:
- selects cells adjacent to outside/zero,
- tries to erase them into color `0`,
- occasionally performs local nonzero recoloring moves to reshape bottlenecks,
- retains the best valid grid found.

This permits substantially more candidate evaluations within the time limit than the prior full connectivity-check approach.
